links.outcome: Model performance across sex-based training configurations and subgroup-specific precision/recall
links.effect: Male-only training gave accuracy 78.2% and F1 0.60 versus 94.5% for female-dominant; male-dominant training showed lower precision for females (0.67) than males (0.80).
links.quote: The male-dominant configuration produced intermediate accuracy (84.1%) but exhibited asymmetric precision/recall across genders, indicating that predictions favoured male samples and were less consistent for female samples.

links.outcome: Effect of sex representation in training data on model performance
links.effect: Male-only data: accuracy 78.2%, RMSE 1.80; female-dominant: accuracy 94.5%, RMSE 0.70. Male-skewed datasets had larger errors and lower success rates.
links.quote: These findings reveal a systematic relationship between demographic representation and error magnitude: male-skewed datasets exhibited larger errors and lower success rates, undermining fairness and reliability.

links.outcome: Bias scores and F1/accuracy after TimeGAN augmentation, equalised-odds regularisation and threshold adjustment
links.effect: Bias reduced to as low as 0.00005 (from 0.0261 in abstract), p<0.001; post-mitigation accuracy 98.5-99.03%, F1 0.975-0.993. TimeGAN raised male-only F1 0.79 to 0.88.
links.quote: Performance remained high across configurations, indicating that bias reduction was achieved without substantial degradation in Accuracy, Precision, Recall, or F1-score.

links.outcome: Fairness and calibration metrics reported across subgroups
links.effect: DI ratios all exceeded 0.8 (1.000-1.165) despite large accuracy/error gaps; log loss 1.25 in male-only versus 0.28 in female-dominant. Mitigation reported without confidence intervals.
links.quote: All DI values exceeded 0.8, indicating compliance with the standard disparate impact threshold; however, female-skewed configurations achieved higher DI values than male-skewed settings.

links.outcome: Performance by gender representation in training data
links.effect: Male-only accuracy 78.2%, RMSE 1.80; balanced accuracy 88.9%, RMSE 1.10; female-dominant accuracy 94.5%, RMSE 0.70.
links.quote: Gender-imbalanced training–particularly male-only data–produced significantly lower accuracy, higher error rates, and poorer agreement with ground truth, whereas balanced or female-majority training improved both predictive accuracy and equity.
